searchText: GM GM EPF Community! just removing it for now to prevent confusions for now why would 1153 be relevant in zkp verification? as far as i understand it, zkp verification is simply an expensive cryptographic operation. i dont see why the computation would be split across multiple contracts ( the main use for 1153 ) as the call overhead would certainly add up also in the doc you have a "specification" section - the purpose of this section is to fully explain a proposal so that an implementer may, with no outside resources, implement the proposal. in your doc it is not clear what the proposal is nor how to implement it Hi everyone, I wrote an article explaining how Lighthouse starts a Beacon Node, focusing on its interactions with the Execution Engine. I hope some of you can find it useful `:)` https://hackmd.io/@danielrachi/S1u2Veflp thanks <@543900561460822016> for the comment, actually i need to provide the whole concept and problem we faced when we thought of stateless relay for Flashbot to make this sub proposal meaningful , ill share entire journey of thoughts with you to make it clear. i could solve my problem in current work with escrow but thought in long term this can be better solution mind if we could set up a call? <@543900561460822016> nice overview of the start up process! > I don’t know how far can a CL client go only with those endpoints. It wont actually go very far unfortunately - i would curious to understand exactly what happens in lighthouse after the initial fcu, but eventually it is going to start sending `newPayloadV2` to the EL. This is how the CL uses the EL to ensure the validity of the execution payload. If you're trying to implement this on a portal client, you will need i) and EVM and ii) to implement state look ups for execution. This might be difficult given the latency of pushing state into portal. I dont on the top of mind remember what the timeout for newpayload is. im not sure there is much use in a call, i would like to see a much more fleshed out idea and spec first before i can provide any constructive feedback Thanks! This is client dependent, we set it at 12 seconds on prysm if I recall correctly, but most probably all Els timeout earlier

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content:
nice overview of the start up process!

> I don’t know how far can a CL client go only with those endpoints.
It wont actually go very far unfortunately - i would curious to understand exactly what happens in lighthouse after the initial fcu, but eventually it is going to start sending `newPayloadV2` to the EL. This is how the CL uses the EL to ensure the validity of the execution payload. If you're trying to implement this on a portal client, you will need i) and EVM and ii) to implement state look ups for execution.

This might be difficult given the latency of pushing state into portal. I dont on the top of mind remember what the timeout for newpayload is.
